classification.difficultyReason: Identify the perpendicular projection onto each of two different planes, calculate a face diagonal and use trigonometry to find each inclination.

content.prompt: In the prism $ABCDEFGH$, $AB=12\text{ cm}$, $BC=5\text{ cm}$ and $CG=6\text{ cm}$. Find, correct to one decimal place:

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular prism with front face ABEF and rear face DCGH displaced upwards and rightwards. AD, DC and DH are hidden dashed edges; the remaining nine edges are solid. Ordinary source blue and red strokes become house black, with dashes preserving hidden-edge meaning.
spec.mathematics: AB=12 cm, BC=5 cm and CG=6 cm are supplied in the stem only. All eight vertices are labelled. Neither AG nor HB is drawn in the question figure.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated diagonal, projected line or inclination angle is supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the inclination of $AG$ to the plane $ABCD$

answer.short:
$24.8^\circ$

Use $AC$, the projection of $AG$ onto the base.
answer.worked:
The perpendicular projection of $G$ onto plane $ABCD$ is $C$, so the required angle is $\angle GAC$. Triangle $ACG$ is right-angled at $C$.

$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=AB^2+BC^2\\AC^2&=12^2+5^2\\AC^2&=169\\AC&=13\text{ cm}\\\tan\angle GAC&=\frac{CG}{AC}\\\tan\angle GAC&=\frac{6}{13}\\\angle GAC&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{6}{13}\right)\\\angle GAC&\approx24.8^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the inclination of $HB$ to the plane $BCGF$

answer.short:
$56.9^\circ$

Use $BG$, the projection of $BH$ onto the side face.
answer.worked:
The perpendicular projection of $H$ onto plane $BCGF$ is $G$, since $HG$ is perpendicular to that face. The required angle is $\angle HBG$, and triangle $BGH$ is right-angled at $G$.

$$\begin{align*}BG^2&=BC^2+CG^2\\BG^2&=5^2+6^2\\BG^2&=61\\BG&=\sqrt{61}\text{ cm}\\HG&=AB=12\text{ cm}\\\tan\angle HBG&=\frac{HG}{BG}\\\tan\angle HBG&=\frac{12}{\sqrt{61}}\\\angle HBG&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{12}{\sqrt{61}}\right)\\\angle HBG&\approx56.9^\circ\end{align*}$$
